question.value: What powers and sustains a giant Lyα nebula in the core of the z=1.99 X-ray cluster CL J1449+0856, and how much energy do galaxy outflows inject into the ICM?

evidence.quote: We investigate the possibility that cluster galaxies supply the required gas through outflows and we show that their total mass outflow rate matches the replenishment necessary to sustain the nebula.
This paper also makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2012.1.00885.S.
or 870 $\mu$m continuum detection in ALMA maps applying a Main-Sequence galaxy template

evidence.quote: We observed CL J1449+0856 (Figure [1](#fig:rgb)) for 3.5 h with the narrow-band filter NB3640 installed in the blue arm of the Keck/LRIS camera on March 27, 2014

provided.value: ACIS-S 94.81 ks follow-up plus archival ACIS-I; cluster and AGN X-ray properties

evidence.quote: In Cycle 16 we followed-up the field with the ACIS-S camera (aimpoint at CCD=7) for a nominal exposure of 94.81 ks in very faint mode.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive SFR of bright ALMA source

method.value: 870 μm flux converted to L_IR and SFR with a Main-Sequence template

evidence.quote: Its 870 $\mu$m flux is $F_{\mathrm{870\mu m}} = 5.5$ mJy, corresponding to a total infra-red luminosity between $8-1000$ $\mu$m of $L_{\mathrm{IR}} = 6.6\times10^{12}$ L$_\odot$

assumptions.value: Source excluded from SFR accounting because membership is unconfirmed

evidence.quote: As there is no spectroscopic confirmation that the ALMA source is a member of the cluster, we have conservatively excluded it from the SFR accounting.

used_for.value: dual-image source detection in narrow- and broad-band optical images

evidence.quote: We selected individual Ly$\alpha$ absorbers and emitters by running SExtractor in dual image mode
reprocessing was carried out using CIAO version 4.6

results_numeric.quantity: 870 μm flux of bright ALMA source

evidence.quote: Its 870 $\mu$m flux is $F_{\mathrm{870\mu m}} = 5.5$ mJy
$L_{\mathrm{Ly\alpha}}=(2.3\pm0.2)\times10^{43}$ erg s$^{-1}$

findings_qualitative.value: AGN are the most plausible power source of the nebula

evidence.quote: The most plausible candidates to power the nebula are two Chandra-detected AGN host cluster members

claims.hypothesis: Galaxy outflows can supply the gas replenishment needed to sustain the nebula
claims.experiment: Summed SFR-based and AGN-based mass outflow rates of core members, including an ALMA 870 μm SFR
claims.result: Total SFR ≈1000 Msun/yr and AGN outflows ≈1400 Msun/yr versus required ≳1000 Msun/yr
claims.finding: Outflows are sufficient and imply ≈2 keV per particle injected into the ICM

evidence.quote: the generous total SFR ($\approx1000$ M$_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$) and the outflow rate owing to the growth of supermassive black holes ($\approx1400$ M$_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$) are sufficient to replenish the nebula

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Young stars, cold flows and classical cooling flows disfavored as the Lyα power source

evidence.quote: disfavoring ionization from very young stars and cooling from the X-ray phase in the form of a stationary classical cooling flow

limitations_admitted.value: ALMA source membership unconfirmed; it would double the core SFR

evidence.quote: if confirmed to be part of the cluster, this source would increase by a factor of $2\times$ the total SFR in the core

referee_caveats_inferred: ALMA contribution is one flux and an SFR with no processing details
The SFR rests on a template conversion
